answer: A call at parameter mf makes s smaller calls at parameter f, each on a stream of volume V/W, so the cost per unit of data C satisfies C(mf) <= (s/W) C(f) + O(1), with C(1) = O(1). Unrolling this over the log_m f levels gives a sum of powers (s/W)^j, and its largest term is (s/W)^(log_m f) = f^(log_m(s/W)) when s/W > 1. Since s/W < m, the exponent log_m(s/W) is strictly below 1, so C(f) = O(f^tau) for any fixed tau < 1 with s/W < m^tau. What must hold: the total rank s of the edge changes must be strictly below W*m, so that s/W = m(1 - eta) for a fixed eta > 0 set by the network; the Pukezad page gets this strict inequality by counting ranks, s_b = W_b m - (N - 2 L_b) with L_b/N = 100/539 < 1/2. How large: the page fixes tau = 1 - 2^(-50), which works once eta > 20 * 2^(-50), and the actual bit-network deficit is eta = 339/22587335000000, about 1.5 * 10^(-11). So the exponent is 1 + log_m(1 - eta), a little below 1. (By my own arithmetic it is about 1 - 10^(-12); that number is not on any page.)

citations.quote: Unrolling $\log_m f$ levels, depth $j$ (the number of levels below the top call, not a stage number) contributes $(s/W)^j$
The deepest term is $(s/W)^{\log_m f}=f^{\log_m(s/W)}$; for $s/W>1$ the geometric sum is a constant times it, and for $s/W\le1$ it is $O(\log f)$.
If $s=Wm$, depth $j$ contributes $m^j$, the sum is about $f$, and the cost is proportional to $Vf$: no saving.
The exponent $\log_m(s/W)=1+\log_m(1-\eta)$ is below $1$ exactly when $\eta>0$, and $\eta$ is fixed with the network.
So any fixed $\tau<1$ with $s/W<m^\tau$ gives $\mathcal C(f)=O(f^\tau)$, and an interchange costs $O(Vf^\tau)$.
Source dimensions sum to $N$, sink dimensions to $Nm+N(m-1)+(W-2N)m=Wm-N$.
Hence $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}m-(N-2L_{\rm b})$ and $s_{\rm c}=W_{\rm c}m-(2N-2L_{\rm c})$, both below $Wm$ because $L_{\rm b}/N=100/539$ and $L_{\rm c}/N=101/539$ are below $1/2$.
For $A$ in a fixed finite set, it can be performed with exactly $a$ interchanges of $b$-digit fields and $O(V)$ further work.
Both exceed $20\cdot2^{-50}\approx1.8\cdot10^{-14}$, by a factor over $200$.
Hence $\tau=\sigma=1-2^{-50}$ gives $s_{\rm b}/W_{\rm b}<m^\tau$ and $s_{\rm c}/W_{\rm c}<m^\sigma$, with $0<\tau=\sigma<1$.

stuck.quote: A call at parameter $mf$ cuts each chunk into $m$ slots of parameter $f$, one per coordinate of the label space.
stuck.note: I followed that a call at mf makes m slots and that an edge costs one interchange per unit of rank. I could not see on this page why the m slots are the same m as the label-space dimension. I got past it only by matching m across pages: the Fizokid page has the frame matrices as m x m, and the Mugumez page gives the label space as F tensor F tensor F of dimension h^3 = m. The page asserts the identification.

stuck.quote: The call deals its rows into $W$ streams of volume $V/W$, one per wire of the bit or complex network, and runs each gate pointwise.
stuck.note: The step that one edge's frame change of rank r is r calls on the same V/W stream is not spelled out. I got past it by assuming each frame change acts only on the array carried by that wire, which the Gepupog page supports only indirectly.

stuck.quote: Comparing entries, every arrow is an inclusion except centre $3\to4$, which drops $P\otimes F\otimes Q$ of dimension $h$
stuck.note: The label table for the gates is given as facts with no derivation. I could check the dimension h of P tensor F tensor Q from the Mugumez page, but I could not tell from this page why these labels are the right ones, so I took the table on trust.

stuck.quote: Every route must change frame in all $m$ dimensions, so if every wire climbed from dimension $0$ to $m$ the total would be exactly $Wm$, which, as shown below, saves nothing.
stuck.note: I could not tell whether 'every route must change frame in all m dimensions' is derived anywhere I opened or is only motivation. The page gives no reason for it.

stuck.quote: The gap $2^{-50}$ is a choice: the chain needs only $20\cdot2^{-50}<\eta$, and a power of two keeps the exponent simple.
stuck.note: The page gives tau = 1 - 2^(-50) as a valid bound, not as the exponent. It never states the actual exponent 1 + log_m(1 - eta) as a number, so 'how large is it' has to be read off eta. I could not tell whether the rounded tau is meant as the answer to 'how large' or only as a bound. I worked out the actual exponent myself, and that is not on any page.

key_idea.statement: Each recursion level multiplies the cost per unit of data by s/W, which is below m, so after log_m f levels the cost is f raised to the power log_m(s/W), a power strictly below the first.
key_idea.quote: The deepest term is $(s/W)^{\log_m f}=f^{\log_m(s/W)}$; for $s/W>1$ the geometric sum is a constant times it, and for $s/W\le1$ it is $O(\log f)$.

reason: Answered. The recurrence on the Pipozop page (rut) gives the exponent log_m(s/W), which is below 1 once s < Wm. The strict inequality is the rank count on the Pukezad page (dol), with L_b/N = 100/539 < 1/2. The explicit size is the page's tau = 1 - 2^(-50) and deficit eta about 1.5e-11. I recomputed L_b/N = 100/539, W_b = (22587335/539) N, and eta_b = 339/22587335000000 by hand, and they agree with the pages. I found no inconsistency. Confidence is moderate: the link between the m of the slots and the m of the label space, and the claim that a frame change touches only one V/W stream, were matched across pages rather than stated on one page. I did not check the complex-network numbers or the Sifigeg and Lilelab pages. I opened 8 of the 15 allowed pages.
